# Independent audit of the optimized-capacity Schur correction

Full read of `candidate a5d3d44181ebed82`: **PASS**.

The three-exponential survival formulas agree through their second w derivatives at zero, including the repeated-positive-parameter limit. Parameter differentiation preserves the matching identities. Their exponential bounds, followed by conditioning on the remaining phases, give the required joint C2 regularity even with zero margins. This justifies the full Hessian rather than only the two chosen coordinate derivatives.

Independently differentiating t P(t1-x)^(-1/d) gives the displayed three Hessian blocks. For a vector v with g dot v=0 and arbitrary l, substitution into the Schur complement simplifies exactly to

    (v+l1)^T Hess(phi)(v+l1)
      =-P^(-1/d)/(dP)
          [v^T H v+(eta dot v-l dP)^2/B].

Therefore l=(eta dot v)/(dP) cancels the entire threshold-optimization loss. The normalizing identities g dot 1=dP and H1 dot 1=d(d-1)P-B account for every factor. The original uncorrected pair direction need not have positive capacity curvature, and the source correctly avoids that inference.

The central-pair input is the proved reciprocal-Laplace cap Hessian lemma; it requires centrality only at the two strictly captured vertices. Repeated margins use the divided-difference limit, already covered by the C2 proof.

The d=3 nondegeneracy argument is sound. A proper minimizing full row has at least two strictly captured vertices. Thus it cannot have two boundary vertices. All relevant triangular-face derivatives are continuous at the threshold: a one-boundary proper face is a usual C1 vertex knot; a full face can only have a single boundary vertex and then its missing area is quadratic. The differentiated facet identity at B=0 forces each face to be stationary for its area-root ratio. Deleting one captured vertex in a two-captured cut leaves a positive-shift vertex cap, whose first derivative contradicts that equality, including an intercept equal to one. Deleting the excluded vertex in a three-captured cut leaves a full face. These cases exhaust all incidences.

Adding the Schur correction's multiple of 1 preserves active-row-span membership, because the columns sum to one. The final rank consequence is accurately scoped: it neither proves that a central captured pair exists in every row nor that its pair vector lies in a rank-three span. The independent joint-index supplement can fund several such row directions together, but that is a separate lemma.

## Added all-dimensional nondegeneracy proof

The new Section 4 also independently **PASSES**. At a full-row stationary threshold normalized to one, every positive margin is strictly less than one. One positive margin alone would give f_V(0)=P/c_positive, contradicting stationarity P=f_V(0). Thus the source's joint C2 three-phase argument applies.

For the actual positive log-concave density f_V, its tangent exponential on the positive halfline implies f_V'(0)/f_V(0)>=-1, because its positive-tail integral equals f_V(0). Equality would force the entire positive tail to be f_V(0)e^(-s), by continuity and equality of the nonnegative integral gap. But all positive margins less than one give a finite exponential moment at some lambda>1, directly from the independent exponential moment product. This rules out equality and yields f_V'(0)>-P.

The sign and factor connecting this to B are correct: simultaneous coefficient shift has second derivative -f_L'(0), and the independent gamma radius has E[G^(-2)]=1/[d(d-1)]. Splitting the density difference quotient at G=|v|/delta controls the small-radius contribution by O(|v|^(d-1)); on the remainder the integrable G^(-2) bound permits dominated convergence. This covers d=2 as well as larger dimensions, and it does not require distinct or nonzero remaining margins. Consequently B=d(d-1)[P+f_V'(0)]>0 in every d>=2, and the central-pair corrected positive capacity direction is unconditional for every proper minimizing full row.

## Added all-dimensional same-side and full-matrix consequence

The new Section 6 also **PASSES**. Size bias gives g_j/f(0) as the stated exponential average of f(-c_js)/f(0). If the log-density slope at zero is nonnegative, logconcavity bounds every such integrand by one on a positive-margin coordinate. A positive-side coordinate exceeding 1/d therefore forces a negative slope. Reversing V gives the incompatible positive-slope requirement for a negative-side noncentral coordinate. Zero margins give exactly 1/d. This proves the same-side assertion under the explicit C1 logconcavity hypothesis, already established for all proper full-row minima.

The full-matrix consequence uses actual common section centroids from weighted gradient equality. Thresholds are b dot row, so their sum is one and every raw-margin column sums to zero. A noncentral coordinate cannot be on any boundary. Consequently some row excludes it and therefore excludes every noncentral coordinate; this row has a captured central pair. The unconditional Schur theorem supplies positive capacity curvature, and full row rank makes the exact projective variation feasible. The proof handles the all-central case directly and does not assert an unsupported extension to deficient active rank.
